title: An Afternoon in the Archive
paragraphs: During an afternoon at a community archive, a class examined records of ordinary experiences. Some came from personal journals, while others resembled reports or scenes from fiction. The students agreed that useful evidence could come from a quiet incident as well as a surprising one.

Several records provided a starting point for the discussion. They had to scrimp for months to afford the trip. The path crossed a dry, scrubby hillside. Do not scrunch the map into the bottom of the bag. She had a scruple about accepting credit for another person's work.

Other records complicated that first impression and encouraged a closer reading. The figures did not withstand close scrutiny. A short scuffle broke out near the entrance. The mice began to scurry beneath the cupboard. The old seafarer described voyages to distant ports.

The class finished by comparing its first impressions with its later interpretations. Some ideas had survived closer examination; others needed to be revised. The students kept the original details visible so that future readers could judge for themselves. They understood that a convincing explanation should connect the evidence clearly while leaving room for questions the records could not answer.

targets.definition: to save money by spending very little
to squeeze or crush into a smaller shape
a doubt or hesitation about whether something is right
to move quickly with short steps
a person who travels or works at sea
